title: Soaring with TRILLI: An HW/SW Heterogeneous Accelerator for Multi-Modal Image Registration
problem: 3D rigid image registration requires compute-intensive geometric transformation with interpolation and similarity metric computation, but existing hardware accelerators cannot address both components effectively since GPUs excel at image transformation while FPGAs dominate in similarity metric computation.
motivation: Rigid image registration dominates the computational cost in medical imaging pipelines where it serves as either a standalone process or critical preprocessing step for non-rigid registration.
method: TRILLI uses a Versal chip that combines a GPU and FPGA to split image registration work. The GPU handles the computationally heavy geometric transformation and interpolation (moving and resizing images to align them), while the FPGA computes similarity metrics (measurements of how well images match). By using each hardware type where it excels, TRILLI creates an end-to-end system that performs better than making one hardware type handle all the work.
key_novelty: TRILLI's core idea is using the GPU for image transformation and the FPGA for similarity metric computation, rather than forcing one hardware type to handle both tasks.
contributions: TRILLI accelerator for image transformation and interpolation on Versal SoC
5.32× speedup over top-performing GPU solutions for transformation and interpolation
36.75× energy efficiency improvement versus most efficient GPU-only approaches
End-to-end rigid registration achieving 18.60× speedup and 36.11× energy efficiency versus best GPU baseline
primary_theme: heterogeneous acceleration for medical image registration
